title: Data Parallelism: Vector Units and GPUs

contract.reader: A programmer who has read entries 1 to 3 and wants to know what vector instructions and GPUs can do for a numerical loop
contract.problem: Predicting whether a loop gains from vectorization or from a GPU, and why
contract.outcome: Read vectorization reports; recognize the five blockers; explain warps, occupancy, coalescing and tiling; estimate when offloading repays the transfer
contract.contribution: One roofline argument carried through CPU lanes, GPU memory and the host link, with a measured CPU half and a closed-form break-even size checked by a script
contract.evidence: Measured kernels with compiler reports and disassembly; offload.py output; Flynn, Hennessy and Patterson, Hwu, Kirk and El Hajj, Lindholm et al., Intel, GCC manual
contract.limitations: No GPU measurement (listings not compiled, figures assumed); CUDA vocabulary; FP64 throughput left to vendor documentation

findings.location: Section 6.2, break-even equation; desktop-light and mobile-light
findings.problem: The equation ends at '≈ 25' at 1280 px (252.6 hidden) and earlier at 360 px
findings.whyItMatters: The section's result reads as a wrong value at desktop width; it is restated as n = 253 in the next sentence
findings.action: Split the equation over two lines in an aligned block
findings.acceptance: At 1280 px the whole equation including 252.6 is visible; at 360 px no line hides the result

findings.problem: The opening quotation mark renders as a closing curly quote before inline math
findings.whyItMatters: Visible typographic slip in the first paragraph
findings.action: Write an opening curly quote in the source or rephrase
findings.acceptance: The phrase renders with an opening quote at the start
